title: Surakarta Sunanate
capsule: The Surakarta Sunanate was established on 20 February 1745 when Pakubuwono II relocated the Mataram court from Kartasura—considered inauspiciously tainted after a Chinese-led rebellion—to the village of Sala (Solo) on the Solo River, an event formalised by the Treaty of Giyanti in 1755 which simultaneously created the rival Sultanate of Yogyakarta. Ruled by sunans of the Pakubuwono line, the Sunanate operated under successive protectorates of the VOC, the Batavian Republic, British East India Company, and the Kingdom of the Netherlands, with its sovereignty progressively curtailed. Three rulers—Pakubuwana VI, X, and XII—were later recognised as National Heroes of Indonesia for their roles in resistance and nationalism. Following Indonesian independence, communist-led agitation prompted the Republic to revoke Surakarta's special region status on 16 June 1946, merging it into Central Java province and ending the Sunanate's political authority.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Sunanate's history is well documented through VOC and Dutch colonial archives as well as Javanese court chronicles (babad); territorial boundaries from 1755 are defined by treaty but internal administrative divisions remain imprecisely mapped.
